situation: A team member hands in a report full of errors.
say: This is not acceptable. Redo the whole thing.
better: The analysis is good, but five numbers are wrong. Can you fix them and add a source for each?
also: Let's go through the errors together, then you can take the fix from there.
weak: Good job, just small small changes.
Who taught you to make reports like this?
why: Be specific about the problem and the fix. Criticise the work, not the person.

situation: You must tell the team their project has been cancelled.
say: Guys, management has decided, nothing we can do, project is scrapped.
better: I have hard news: the Pune project is cancelled. I'll explain why, and what it means for each of you.
also: The project has been stopped. I know that's disappointing. Let's talk about what comes next.
weak: Don't worry, it's nothing big, some changes are happening.
Top management messed up again, as usual.
why: Say it plainly, own it as the leader, and move to what's next.

situation: You're handing a task to someone on your team.
say: Do this ASAP and let me know.
better: Can you own the vendor shortlist? I need three options with prices by Thursday. Ask me if you get stuck.
also: This one's yours: three vendor options by Thursday. Shout if you need help.
weak: Just see whatever you can do on the vendors.
Do it, but check with me before every single step.
why: A clear owner, a clear result and a clear deadline, with help on offer.

situation: A team member calmed down an angry client really well.
say: Good job, keep it up.
better: Kavya, the way you handled that angry client was calm and clear. That's why we kept the account.
also: The client mentioned your follow-up, Kavya. Great work.
weak: Nice. Anyway, next thing.
You are the best, the rest of the team should learn from you.
why: Praise the exact action so they know what to repeat. Don't compare.

situation: Someone on your team has missed three deadlines in a row.
say: Why are you always late? This is the third time.
better: Your last three deadlines slipped. What's getting in the way? I want to help fix it.
also: I've noticed a pattern with deadlines. Can we talk about what's happening?
weak: It's okay, no problem, take your time.
If this continues, think about your future here.
why: Name the pattern, then ask before you judge.

situation: The same two people do all the talking in your team meetings.
say: Anyone else? No? Okay, moving on.
better: Before we decide, I'd like to hear from people who haven't spoken yet. Divya, what do you think?
also: Let's go round the table: one thought each.
weak: Why are you all so quiet? Say something.
Okay, then I'll decide, as usual.
why: Invite quiet voices by name. Silence isn't agreement.

situation: You've made a decision that part of the team argued against.
say: This is final. No more discussion.
better: I've heard the concerns, and I've decided to go with the new tool. Here's why, and how we'll handle the risks.
also: Not everyone agrees, and that's okay. We're going ahead, and I'll own the outcome.
weak: Management wants it, so we have to do it.
Let's try both and see, maybe, I don't know.
why: Show you listened, give the reason, and own the decision.

situation: A team member's mistake has caused the website to go down.
say: Who did this? Such a silly mistake!
better: Let's fix the outage first. Tomorrow we'll look at what went wrong, without blaming anyone.
also: First the fix, then the lessons. No finger-pointing.
weak: Rahul, this was your mistake, and everyone should know it.
These things happen, let's just forget about it.
why: Fix first, learn later. Blame teaches people to hide mistakes.

situation: Someone asks for leave during launch week, and you can't spare them.
say: Leave is not possible now, sorry.
better: I can't approve next week because it's launch week. Could you take the week after? I'll make sure you get it.
also: Next week is tough with the launch. Would the 20th work instead?
weak: Leave? Now? Are you serious?
Okay fine, go, we'll manage somehow.
why: Give the reason and offer another date.

situation: You're starting a one-to-one meeting with a team member.
say: So, all good? Any issues?
better: What's one thing that would make your work easier this month?
also: How are you finding the workload these days, honestly?
weak: Everything is fine na? Okay, good.
If there are any problems, tell HR.
why: Open questions get real answers. 'All good?' just gets 'yes'.

situation: The team missed its sales target and spirits are low.
say: We failed. Everyone needs to work harder.
better: We missed the target by 12%. Let's look at what we can control and pick two things to change.
also: Missing it hurts. Let's learn from it, not beat ourselves up.
weak: It's okay, targets don't really matter.
If we miss again, there will be consequences.
why: Be honest about the miss and point to concrete next steps.

situation: You gave the team the wrong deadline, and it caused a rush.
say: Some miscommunication happened from somewhere.
better: That was my mistake. I gave you the old deadline. I'm sorry, and here's how I'm fixing it.
also: I got this wrong. Thanks for flagging it so quickly.
weak: Mistakes were made, let's move on.
Actually, the client confused all of us.
why: When leaders own mistakes, it becomes safe for everyone else to own theirs.

situation: Two people on your team keep clashing and the rest are noticing.
say: You both are adults, sort it out yourselves.
better: I'd like to hear each of you, one at a time, and then agree on how you'll work together.
also: Let's sit together. Each of you says what you need from the other.
weak: Whose fault is it? Tell me quickly.
Just ignore each other and do your work.
why: Stay neutral, hear both sides, and focus on working together.

situation: Your boss wants to give your already-busy team one more project.
say: Okay sir, my team will manage.
better: We can take this, but the app release would slip by two weeks. Is that okay?
also: My team is at full capacity. What should we drop to make room?
weak: Yes sir, no problem, we'll do overtime.
Impossible, my team is already dying.
why: Protect your team by showing the cost, not by flatly refusing.

situation: A senior team member keeps talking over the juniors.
say: You are very dominating in meetings.
better: In today's meeting you finished Anu's sentences twice. I'd like her to have room to speak. Can you watch for that?
also: I've noticed the juniors go quiet when you jump in. Could you give them more room?
weak: Some people are feeling you are rude.
From now on, please stay quiet in meetings.
why: Describe what you saw them do, not a label like 'dominating'.

situation: A team member didn't get the promotion they were hoping for.
say: Management didn't approve, next time for sure.
better: You didn't get the promotion this cycle. I want to be clear about why, and what would get you there next time.
also: It's a no this time. Let's agree on two goals that make your case for next round.
weak: Next time 100%, don't worry.
Others were simply better than you.
why: Be honest, give reasons, and show a path. Don't promise what you can't.

situation: A new person has just joined your team.
say: Just observe for some days, you'll understand.
better: For your first two weeks, shadow Imran and read the docs. From week three, you'll own the small bug fixes.
also: Here's what success looks like in your first month.
weak: Do whatever, you'll pick it up.
We expect you to deliver from day one, no excuses.
why: Clear early goals help new people settle in and do well.

situation: Your team is worried by rumours of a company restructuring.
say: I can't share anything, it's confidential.
better: I don't have all the answers yet. I'll tell you what I know by Friday, and I won't hide bad news.
also: Honestly, nothing is decided. When it is, you'll hear it from me first.
weak: Don't listen to rumours, everything is perfect.
Even I don't know what's going on in this place.
why: Honest uncertainty builds more trust than false comfort.

situation: A team member keeps arriving after the daily 10 o'clock stand-up.
say: Office timing is 9:30, not 10:30. Be serious.
better: You've been coming in after 10 most days. Is something going on? We need you at the stand-up.
also: Mornings seem hard lately. Can we find a fix that still gets you to the stand-up?
weak: Late again? Very nice.
Come whenever you want, just finish the work.
why: Ask about the reason, but be clear about what you need.

situation: You want ideas from the team on a stubborn problem.
say: Any suggestions? Tell me if anything.
better: We need to cut our response time by half. What's one idea you'd try first?
also: No idea is too small. Let's list everything, then pick.
weak: I've already decided, but any suggestions?
Suggestions are welcome, but don't waste my time.
why: A clear problem and a direct question bring out real ideas.

situation: A team member tells you their workload has become too much.
say: Everyone is busy, adjust a little.
better: Thanks for telling me. Let's go through your list together and see what can move or be dropped.
also: That sounds like too much. What would help most right now?
weak: In my time we worked 14 hours a day.
Okay, I'll look into it sometime.
why: Take the concern seriously and act on it together.

situation: A team member suggests an idea you can't afford right now.
say: This won't work. Next.
better: I like the thinking, but we don't have the budget this quarter. Can you keep it ready for April?
also: Not now, because of the budget, but it's a good idea. Let's revisit it in April.
weak: Interesting. Let's see.
And who will pay for all this?
why: Say no to the idea with a reason, and still value the person behind it.

situation: Your team has just shipped a big launch on time.
say: Thanks team for all the efforts.
better: We shipped on time because of Sana's testing and Ravi's late-night fixes. Thank you, all of you.
also: Proud of this team. Lunch is on me on Friday.
weak: Good. Now let's focus on the next release.
Thanks to all for your kind co-operation.
why: Name what people did. Generic thanks feels like a formality.

situation: A client has pulled the deadline four days earlier.
say: Client has preponed the deadline, so adjust accordingly.
better: The client moved the deadline to Monday. That's tight. Let's decide today what we can cut.
also: Bad news: we've lost four days. Here's my plan; tell me what I'm missing.
weak: Client has preponed, so everyone cancel your weekend plans.
Don't panic, but this is a total disaster.
why: Share the facts, admit it's hard, and lead with a plan.

situation: A team member's work has stayed poor despite earlier talks.
say: This is your last chance, otherwise HR will take action.
better: Your work isn't at the level we need. Here are three things that must change in 60 days, and how I'll help.
also: I want you to succeed here, so I'm being direct: these three things need to change.
weak: Try to improve a little, okay?
Honestly, I don't know why we hired you.
why: Serious problems need clear goals and real support, not threats.
